These appeals are arising out of common judgment and award dated 04.09.2018 passed in MVC.Nos.1161 and 2780 of 2015 on the file of X Additional District and Member of Additional MACT, Belagavi ("the Tribunal" for short), they are heard together and dispose off by this common judgment.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to as they are referred to in the claim petitions before the Tribunal.

3. MFA.No.104376/2019 is filed by the claimant seeking enhancement of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, whereas, MFA.No.104377/2018 is filed by the Insurer of the offending vehicle seeking reduction of compensation awarded by the Tribunal and also challenging the liability fastened on the Insurance Company.

4. Brief facts of the claimant's case are as under:
On 13.11.2015 at about 10.30 a.m., one Maruti Birsiddappa Singari, the driver of Toofan Trax bearing registration No.KA.49/M-1287, drove the same in high speed rash and negligent manner on Hukkeri-Sankeshwar road from NC:
2024:KHC-D:7847 Hukkeri to Sankeshwar.
When he came near Kamatnur Gate, he abruptly took left turn to avoid a group of sheep, which came across the road and as a result he lost control over his vehicle and hit against the road side tree.
Due to said impact, the claimant sustained injuries.
5. Considering the oral and documentary evidence on record, the Tribunal granted compensation of Rs.2,24,000/-.

Aggrieved by the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal, the claimant preferred MFA.No.104376/2019 seeking enhancement and the Insurance Company preferred MFA.No.104377/2018 seeking reduction of compensation and also challenging the liability.

6. Learned counsel for the claimant contended that, the Tribunal has not considered the nature of injury and the expenditure incurred by the claimant towards medical expenses and the Tribunal has not at all considered the income of the claimant.
Further the Tribunal has not at all awarded fair and reasonable compensation under the head of pain and suffering, loss of future earning, loss of Mahadev S/O Dundappa Kumbar vs Shri.

7.

Learned counsel for the Insurance Company taken contention that the Tribunal ought to have looked into the fact that the seating capacity of the offending vehicle is 12 passengers, as per the insurance policy.

At the time of accident, 18 paid passengers were travelling in the said vehicle,
thereby the owner of the offending vehicle violated the relevant provisions of Motor Vehicles Act,
1988 ("the MV Act"
for short) and also the terms of the policy.

Learned counsel for the Insurance Company fairly submitted that in a connected matter i.e., MFA.No.104376/2018 filed by the Insurance Company, the Insurance Company withdrew the appeal filed by it and accepted the liability.
His submission is placed on record.

8. In view of the submission made by learned counsel for both the parties, the following points that would arise for consideration by this Court are as follows:
i. Whether the Insurance Company proved that respondent No.1, the owner of the offending vehicle violated the policy condition as contended by the Insurance Company?
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable or does it call for any interference by this Court?
9. The Insurance Company has taken a contention that the owner of the offending vehicle has violated the policy condition.
From the perusal of the policy, the capacity of the vehicle is 12 passengers but as on the date of accident, the driver allowed 18 paid passengers to travel in the offending vehicle.
10. In order to substantiate its contention, the Insurance Company examined its Assistant Manager of the Company as RW.1.

In his evidence, he reiterated the contention taken by the Insurance Company and in support of his contention, relied upon Ex.R.1-Authorisation Letter, Ex.R.2- Insurance Policy, Ex.R.3-Deposition in MVC.No.779/2015, Ex.R.4-Authoriation Letter and Ex.R.5-CD.
11.

In the cross-examination, RW.1 clearly admitted that the Insurance Company has conducted independent investigation in relation to the accident, but the company has not produced the investigation report before the Court.
He has categorically admitted that, the claimant was traveling in the Trax Toofan by paying money.
Further the Insurance Company NC: 2024:KHC-D:7847 has also examined one Ankush as RW.2.
He also reiterated the averments made in the written statement of Insurance Company.
He corroborates the oral testimony of RW.1.

Apart from the oral evidence,
the Insurance Company has not furnished any documents to show that the term of policy conditions were violated.

4 12.
On the other hand, in order to prove the contention of the claimant, the claimant himself examined on oath as PW.1 and relied upon Exs.P.1 to P13.

From perusal of Ex.P.1- FIR,
Ex.P.2-Complaint, Ex.P.3-Spot Panchanama, Ex.P.6- Charge sheet, which establish that on the date of accident, the claimant was travelling in the offending vehicle.
As per Ex.R.2, the insurance was valid as on the date of accident and the offending vehicle stands in the name of respondent No.1.
Since respondent No.1-owner of the offending vehicle has violated the policy condition, the Tribunal held that the Insurance Company is not liable to pay compensation.
On the contrary, the owner of the offending vehicle is liable to pay the compensation.

In view of the ratio laid down in the case of Mukund Dewangan Vs. Oriental Insurance Company Limited and others1, the insurer is liable to pay compensation on account of negligence caused by the driver of the offending vehicle, in view of pay and recovery principle as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Swarn Singh and others2 and also in the case of Rani and others Vs. National Insurance Company Limited and others3.

sentences.text: The breach of the policy must be fundamental in nature that it brings the contract to an end.
It must be established that the accident was, in fact, caused on account of rash and negligent driving by its driver.
The Hon'ble Apex Court was considering the case of the passengers travelling in the vehicle beyond the permitted load/seating capacity.

Six passengers were carried in the vehicle at the time of occurrence of the accident when the permitted load in the vehicle was only 1+1, the insurer contended that there was violation of terms and conditions of insurance policy, as such not liable to indemnify the owner.
In that context, it was held that the excess passengers carried in a vehicle by itself would not be construed as breach on the part of the owner/insured of the vehicle.

Moreover, when the charge sheet was filed against the driver of the opposite vehicle.
11.

In the case of Sri. Anjanappa's case (supra), the Division Bench of this Court had an occasion to consider the provisions of Section 128 of the Act and the Rule 123 of the CMV Rules and 143 of the KMV Rules vis-a-vis claim made while the deceased carrying two pillions on the motorcycle.
It was almost same set of facts as the case on hand, it was held merely breach of law or duty would not create a liability to pay damages.

Merely because the deceased was riding motorcycle with two persons on the vehicle though amounts to contravention of Section 128 of the Act, it does not amount to negligent act on the part of the deceased.

The rider riding the vehicle, if it is - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:7847 demonstrated lost control of the vehicle, he was not able to balance the vehicle or because of such contravention he dashed against the vehicle which resulted in accident,
then the question of extent of breach of duty resulted in negligence would be analysed.
30% of contributory negligence foisted on the deceased solely on the ground that he was riding the motorcycle with two persons behind him was held to be not permissible in law.

The Police documents placed on record was considered to be reliable evidence which were prepared in discharge of their official duty and in the process of investigation, in the absence of any motive being attributed.
This Judgment is squarely applicable to the facts of the present case.
12. Following the above Judgments, it would be held that even assuming that the injured was a pillion itself would not disentitle the claimant from claiming compensation.
13. XXXXX 14.
Thus, Ex.R1 do not instill any evidentiary value much against the Police records which clearly speaks that the vehicle in question was driven by the injured.
The Police Authorities in discharge of their official duty after thorough investigation have prepared the reports, which cannot be overlooked and the same has to be construed as a reliable evidence.

Secondly, violation of Section 128 of the Act and relevant Rules would be amenable to punitive action but that itself would not result in breach of terms and conditions of the insurance policy, the Corporation cannot escape the liability on these grounds.

After hearing the learned counsel for the parties and after perusal of the judgment and award of the Tribunal, I am of the opinion that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is not just and reasonable, it is on lower side and hence, it requires to be enhanced.
17.
The Tribunal considering the grievous injury sustained by the claimant awarded a sum of Rs.30,000/-.
From perusal of Ex.P.5-Wound certificate, the claimant sustained fracture of proximal shaft left bone.
Hence, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is not reasonable one.

Thus,
additional sum of Rs.10,000/- is awarded under the head pain and suffering.
18. The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.28,000/- towards loss of income during the laid up period, considering the income at Rs.7,000/- per month for four months, which is excessive one.
The accident is of the year 2015 and the notional income is taken at Rs.8,000/- per month.

As per the Circular issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority and High Court Legal Services Committee, which comes to - 12 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:7847 Rs.24,000/- for three months (Rs.8,000 X 3 months). Hence, Rs.4,000/- is reduced under this head.

19. Towards loss of future income is concerned, the Tribunal considering the income at Rs.7,000/-
per month, applying the multiplier at "15" and functional disability at 10% awarded a sum of Rs.1,26,000/-, which is not reasonable one.

If monthly income is taken at Rs.8,000/-, applying the multiplier "15" as the claimant was aged 40 years as on the date of accident, and taking 10%
functional disability, the loss of future earnings would be Rs.1,44,000/- (Rs.8,000/- X 12 X 15 X 10%).
20.

The Tribunal has awarded a compensation of Rs.25,000/- under the head of loss of amenities,
which is not reasonable one.
Hence, additional sum of Rs.5,000/- is awarded under this head.
21. Towards medical expenses, the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.10,000/-, which is reasonable one and hence no interference is called for in that regard.

Thus, Ex.R1 do not instill any evidentiary value much against the Police records which clearly speaks that the vehicle in question was driven by the injured.
The Police Authorities in discharge of their official duty after thorough investigation have prepared the reports, which cannot be overlooked and the same has to be construed as a reliable evidence.
Secondly, violation of Section 128 of the Act and relevant Rules would be amenable to punitive action but that itself would not result in breach of terms and conditions of the insurance policy, the Corporation cannot escape the liability on these grounds.
Hence, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is not reasonable one.
